definition: An Asian option settles against the average price of the underlying over a defined period, rather than a single price observed at expiration.
core_idea: Averaging prices over time dampens the impact of any single day's price manipulation or abnormal move, making the option's settlement more resistant to gaming near expiration.
key_points: Commonly used in markets like crude oil where reducing sensitivity to expiration-day manipulation or noise is valuable.
trading_implications: Chosen specifically to reduce settlement risk from price manipulation or one-off spikes on the expiration date.
